If you were born as Al Capone

Chicago 1926 at night: young adult Al in his pearl-grey fedora and pinstriped suit, three scars on his left cheek, stands on a wet street under a streetlamp, smoke curling from his cigar, the city skyline glowing behind him, gangsters' cars parked in the shadows.

Interior of a 1926 small-town restaurant moments after a machine-gun attack: shattered front windows, bullet-pocked walls, overturned chairs, coffee cups spilled, smoke and dust drifting in hard sunlight; young adult Al calmly standing up from behind a table, brushing glass off his suit.

Close-up on a 1920s United States income tax return form lying on a dark wooden desk under a green banker's lamp, a fountain pen beside it; the header reads exactly FORM 1040, nothing else legible; dramatic warm light and deep shadows.

A newborn baby with a tuft of dark hair asleep in a wooden crib in a poor Brooklyn tenement room in winter 1899; frost on the window, through which the cranes and ships of the Brooklyn Navy Yard are visible; a candle glows on a shelf.
1893: a young Italian couple with a small bundle of belongings stands at the rail of a crowded steamship entering New York harbor at dawn, misty city ahead, hopeful and tired faces.
Your dad, Gabriele, is a barber

A small Brooklyn barber shop in 1905: a gentle mustached Italian barber in a white coat carefully shaves a customer with a straight razor, steady hands, warm morning light through the window, bottles and mirrors, little boy Al watching from a stool.
Night in a tiny tenement room: an Italian mother sews a dress by an oil lamp while many small children sleep piled in two beds behind her; boy Al peeks out from under a blanket.
1905 Brooklyn tenement kitchen at night, boy Al sits at a worn table with a schoolbook, grinning and proud, mother at the iron stove behind him, laundry on a line, city lights through the window.
You're fourteen, in the sixth grade
1913 Brooklyn classroom with wooden desks: a stern woman teacher has just slapped teenage Al, age 14, who stands up from his desk with a furious face, fist clenched; shocked classmates stare.
Teenage Al, age 14, walking alone away from a brick school building down a busy Brooklyn street in 1913, hands in pockets, cap low, pushcarts and horse wagons around, late afternoon light.

A Brooklyn street corner at dusk, 1913: Johnny Torrio in his clean dark three-piece suit and bowler hat stands calm and still among rough men in shirtsleeves; boy Al watches him from a doorway, fascinated.
Boy Al running through a narrow alley between tenements at dusk clutching a thick envelope, laundry lines overhead, a cat jumping away, golden window light.
Inside a dim back office with a desk and a safe: Johnny Torrio gently straightens teenage Al's collar and tie like a mentor, Al looking up seriously; a single desk lamp, cigar smoke.
Teenage Al, age 16, with a gang of tough Five Points boys in caps under a New York elevated train track at night, steam rising from a grate, sparks from the train above.

Exterior of a rowdy Coney Island bar and dance hall at night in 1917, strings of bulbs, a glowing amusement park ferris wheel behind, people in 1917 clothes going in, the sea in the distance. No readable signs.
Young Al, age 18, heavyset, behind a crowded wooden bar pouring drinks, rolled sleeves, apron, a bouncer's confident grin, smoky warm interior with a piano player.
In the smoky bar, young Al, age 18, leans over a table smirking at a young woman in a 1917 dress, who looks offended; her brother, a lean young man, glares and starts to stand up.

Tense close-up: a lean young man in a cap with a furious face swings a small knife toward the camera in a dark smoky bar, the blade catching the light, motion blur, dramatic red-orange backlight. No blood.

Young Al, age 18, sits in a back room pressing a white cloth to his LEFT cheek, staring at himself in a cracked mirror, three thin red lines visible on his cheek, shocked expression, single bulb light. Not gory.
A 1920s newspaper photographer with a big flash camera; young Al turns the RIGHT side of his face toward the camera, hiding the scarred left cheek with his hand and hat; flash bulb glare.
fighting in the war in France

In a bar, young Al, age 20, tells an exaggerated war story to amazed listeners, gesturing proudly at his scarred cheek; behind him a dreamy sepia vision of World War One trenches and smoke, clearly imaginary.
Young adult Al in his grey suit shakes hands with the lean young man who once cut him, who now wears a bodyguard's dark suit and holster, awkward smiles, in front of a black 1920s car.
You meet a quiet Irish girl
1918 dance hall, soft lights: young Al, nervous and smiling, meets Mae, a shy auburn-haired Irish girl, who smiles back; couples dancing blurred around them.
A small bedroom in December 1918, snow at the window: Mae holds a newborn baby wrapped in a blanket, young Al leans over them with a huge tender smile.
Sonny gets a terrible ear infection
A 1920 hospital room: a little boy with a bandage wrapped around his head sleeps in a white iron bed; young Al sits at the bedside holding his small hand, worried; dim window light.

A Baltimore construction company office in 1919: young Al in shirt sleeves and arm garters at a desk covered in ledgers and an adding machine, totting up numbers with a pencil, focused, morning light.
An empty barber shop at dusk, 1920: the barber chair stands empty, a folded straight razor and a white coat lie on the counter, a black mourning ribbon on the mirror, dust in the last light.
Close-up of young Al's hands opening a letter on a kitchen table, an envelope postmarked Chicago, lamplight, his scarred cheek just visible in soft focus.
1920: young Al steps off a steam train onto a busy Chicago station platform carrying a suitcase, steam everywhere, the city skyline beyond the station roof, determined look.
1920 Chicago street: police officers pour barrels of whiskey into the gutter while a crowd watches glumly; the liquid runs in streams down the street.
A packed secret 1920s speakeasy behind a fake shop wall: jazz band, flapper dancers, cocktails, hidden doorway with a peephole, warm golden light and haze.
Night, 1922 Chicago: a convoy of trucks loaded with beer barrels drives past a policeman who looks away while pocketing an envelope of cash, wet cobblestones, streetlights.
Close-up of young Al's hand with a diamond ring holding out a small printed business card that reads exactly: ALPHONSE CAPONE  SECOND HAND FURNITURE DEALER. Soft background of an office.
Cicero, 1924 election day: a polling place on a small-town street with armed men in suits and caps standing by the door, nervous voters lined up, cars and smoke, overcast sky.
they kill your big brother Frank
Aftermath on a street at dusk: young Al kneels in grief beside a fallen man's hat on the pavement, police cars in the distance, flickering streetlight. No blood.
A 1924 Chicago flower shop interior full of bouquets and wreaths, a carnation dropped on the floor, a door left swinging, ominous cold light from the street.
Winter night, 1925: a car speeds away from a brownstone house, gun smoke hanging in the air, Johnny Torrio's bowler hat lying in the snow, a woman screaming in the doorway.
A hospital room: Johnny Torrio, bandaged and pale in bed, presses a ring of keys into young Al's hand; Al stands in his grey suit and fedora, serious.
Young adult Al stands at a tall hotel window at night looking out over a glittering 1925 Chicago skyline, back to camera, cigar smoke, reflection of his face in the glass.
Young adult Al in a bright lavender-grey suit, diamond ring, pearl-grey fedora, laughing, stepping out of a black armored 1920s limousine, bodyguards around him, flashbulbs.
A smoky back room: young adult Al hands thick envelopes of cash to a policeman and a man in a judge's robe across a card table, everyone smiling.
A quiet sunny small-town street in Cicero, 1926, viewed through a restaurant window from inside: young adult Al eats lunch at a table, while outside a slow line of black cars rolls up to the curb.
Exterior street view: gunmen fire Tommy guns from the windows of black 1920s cars at a restaurant front, muzzle flashes, glass exploding, dust and smoke, dramatic action, no bodies.
Inside the restaurant during the attack: a bodyguard in a dark suit throws himself on top of young Al on the floor under a table, glass raining down, light beams through bullet holes.
To the papers, you're a monster.
Split scene: on the left, a shadowy villainous Al silhouette on a newspaper front page; on the right, poor Chicago families cheering Al in the street. No readable text.
A sunny 1929 Miami island mansion with palm trees, a swimming pool and a dock on turquoise water; young adult Al in a straw hat and white shirt relaxing in a lounge chair.
Snowy Chicago street, February 1929, morning: a black police car parks in front of a brick garage; men in police uniforms and long coats step out, breath steaming.
Inside a cold brick garage: seven fedoras lying on the concrete floor in front of a bullet-pocked brick wall, gun smoke drifting in a shaft of light. No people, no blood.
A man in a heavy overcoat and fedora stops on a snowy sidewalk, sees a police car down the street, and turns to walk away, his face in shadow.
1929 Oval Office: President Herbert Hoover, stern, sits at his desk reading a newspaper about Chicago gangsters, grey morning light.
Night raid: a heavy truck with a steel ram smashes through the wooden doors of a hidden brewery, beer barrels bursting, a young agent in a hat leading armed agents, flashlights.
What gets you is a book.
Close-up of an old cloth-bound ledger opened under a desk lamp, columns of handwritten numbers, a gloved finger pointing at an entry, cigarette smoke.
1930 Chicago in winter: a long line of hungry men in coats waits outside a soup kitchen, steam from the doorway, volunteers handing out bowls; young adult Al watches from a car window.
1931 wood-paneled federal courtroom: young adult Al in a suit at the defense table, a stern judge with bushy eyebrows above, jurors in the box, reporters behind.
Close-up: young adult Al's stunned face in the courtroom, light from tall windows, his lawyer's hand on his shoulder, reporters rushing out in the background.
Alcatraz island prison in San Francisco Bay at dusk, fog rolling in, lighthouse beam, cold blue water, a prison boat approaching.
Alcatraz cell block: Al, now 35, in a plain grey prison uniform, mops the polished concrete floor alone, long rows of cells and harsh overhead light.
Alcatraz recreation room: Al in prison uniform plays a banjo with a small band of inmates with a trumpet and a drum, a faint smile, warm light from a high window.
Al, age 39, sits alone on his prison bunk in a dark cell staring at the wall, faint ghostly shapes of men in fedoras in the shadows, cold moonlight through the bars.
Golden sunset on the Miami mansion dock: old Al in striped pajamas and a robe sits fishing with a rod, the pool and palm trees behind him, calm water.
Old Al in pajamas stands in a sunny living room pointing and talking firmly to empty armchairs, Mae watching sadly from the doorway.
A dim bedroom with a soft dawn light: old Al lies in bed, Mae holds his hand, his grown son stands beside them, a crucifix on the wall. Peaceful, not grim.
An empty old barber chair in a pool of warm light, a folded straight razor on the seat beside a pearl-grey fedora, dark background.
Portrait of young adult Al in his fedora and pinstriped suit, half his face in warm light and half in deep shadow, looking straight at the viewer, cigar smoke.
